messages:
noah: Hi everyone, happy to be here! First-day setup Qs: mac M2, brew + asdf for node/python, using 1Password SSH agent for keys, and direnv for env vars. Two problems: 1) asdf-installed node sometimes not picked up by VS Code terminal; 2) git commit signing via gpg isn't working because I use 1Password's gpg agent. Any quick recipes?

rachel: welcome! For VS Code make sure you open the folder with the regular app (not the system one under Rosetta). Add asdf init to both ~/.zprofile and ~/.zshrc to catch login and interactive shells, or add `-l` to terminal shell args.

noah: I already put asdf init in .zshrc but vscode still shows node missing until I restart window. Is that expected?

ton y: sometimes the extension host caches PATH. Workarounds: 1) in settings.json add `terminal.integrated.shellArgs.osx: ['-l']`, 2) symlink ~/.asdf to the workspace and source shims from .envrc, or 3) install runtimes via brew in CI image. We usually prefer direnv to export PATH so the terminal picks it up without full restart.

rachel: about 1Password: set `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` to the 1Password agent socket and export it in your shell rc. For GPG signing, 1Password has a SSH/GPG agent integration; point git to use `gpg.program` that calls the 1Password gpg wrapper. If you want, I can paste the small gpg wrapper we use.

noah: that'd be great. Also curious: any repo-level .envrc template so I don't accidentally leak API keys?

ton y: we keep a repo template at scripts/.envrc.template that loads only non-sensitive variables and sources secrets from ~/.local/secrets. Use `direnv allow` after editing. Onboarding checklist mentions adding your SSH key to GitHub org if gpg is delayed.

onboard-bot: Reminder: complete "dev env configured" step on onboarding tracker: https://redwood.example.com/onboarding/12345

noah: thanks! I'll add my SSH key to the org and ping rachel for the gpg wrapper if I hit issues. Appreciate the warm welcome :smile:
